text.text_excerpt: The Zulu parade was a great parade for so many reasons. First, we totally lucked out on parking. I was driving the Yaris and managed to squeeze into a spot about 1 block from the parade route. Yippee! We arrived at 7:15 and planned to watch the parade on Jackson Avenue by Lasalle. Not the greatest area, but smaller crowds. Even though I'm sure the krewe was trying to conserve most of their throws for the St Charles crowd, they were really generous and had some super unique stuff. Of course, the coveted coconuts - we got 2, and one of the half-shell beads too. They were all very into the parade, which is good - I've seen some unenthusiastic float riders in my time. 5 Stars are well deserve...

This is the real address for ZULU and this review is for the ACTUAL Social Aid and Pleasure Club, NOT the parade. This organization has been around since 1909 a group of laborers who had organized a club named "The Tramps," went to the Pythian Theater to see a musical comedy performed by the Smart Set. The comedy included a skit entitled, "There Never Was and Never Will Be a King Like Me," about the Zulu Tribe... and ZULU Social Aid and Pleasure Club was born. The Zulu Social Aid & Pleasure Club Inc., is an every man's club. The membership is composed of men from all walks of life-from laborers, City Mayor, City Councilmen, and State Legislators, to United States Congressman, educators, a...

More good done by any other Carnival Krewe in the region, Zulu shines above all rivals. All Hail, Zulu King!
